text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Westamarin shipyard in Kristiansand in southern Norway, was declared bankrupt on Tuesday. About 500 employees will lose their jobs.

- Grocery and investment group Hakon-Gruppen will open its first supermarket in the Lithuanian capital of Riga in a few months. Head of Hakon-Gruppen, Stein-Erik Hagen, says the company plans to establish a couple of branches in Riga.

- International software house Sysdeco ASA issued a profit warning on Tuesday. Sysdeco said it expected a significant loss when it publishes third quarter results in November. Shares in Sysdeco fell 20 percent on Tuesday before the profit warning was released and trading was suspended on the Oslo bourse.
- Shipyard Kvaerner Fjllstrand may buy the bankrupt Westamarin shipyard in Kristiansand in southern Norway. Kvaerner Fjellstrand expects to run at a profit in 1997.

- The Fisheries Ministry's concession allowing Resource Group International (RGI) to buy Norwegian seafood group Melbu Fiskeindustrier is dependent upon the ministry's approval of any changes in shareholding in RGI. The ruling is in accordance with a law allowing the ministry to have some control over who owns Norwegian fishing boats.
